meaning:
1) (Qal) to heap up, pile up
1a) of grain, dust, silver

elsewhere.note: Let them gather all the food of these good years that come, and store grain under the hand of Pharaoh for food in the cities, and let them keep it.
They gathered them together in heaps, and the land stank.
Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare clothing as the clay;
“Surely every man walks like a shadow. Surely they busy themselves in vain. He heaps up, and doesn’t know who shall gather.
Yes, he scoffs at kings, and princes are a derision to him. He laughs at every stronghold, for he builds up an earthen ramp, and takes it.
Tyre built herself a stronghold, and heaped up silver like the dust, and fine gold like the mire of the streets.
